title: Tube feeding and gastrostomy feeding at home
what: If a person cannot eat by mouth, food is given through a thin tube, either through the nose to the stomach or straight into the stomach through the belly. At home, family members do this.
why: For swallowing problems after a stroke, for diseases of the throat and food pipe, and other conditions when the doctor has ordered this kind of feeding.
duration: one feeding usually takes 20 to 40 minutes, or several hours if given slowly by pump
tell_doctor: If there is vomiting, bloating, diarrhea or constipation
If the skin around the gastrostomy is red, weeping or sore
If the tube has moved or looks shorter on the outside
If the person coughs during feeding

prepare.title: Formula
prepare.text: The doctor prescribes which formula, how much and how often. Do not change it yourself.

prepare.title: Temperature
prepare.text: Give the formula at room temperature, not cold and not hot.

prepare.title: Position
prepare.text: Raise the person's head and chest, sitting or half sitting.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Not all tablets can go through the tube. Ask the doctor or pharmacist which can be crushed.

bring: The formula and a feeding syringe
Discharge papers with the feeding plan
A spare tube or adapter, if you were given one
steps: Wash your hands and prepare the formula
Sit the person up or raise the head of the bed
Check the tube is in place, using the mark on the tube
Flush the tube with a small amount of water
Give the formula slowly, with a syringe or a pump
Flush the tube with water again after feeding
Keep the person half sitting for at least another 30 minutes
feel: It can feel strange to the person, sometimes with a feeling of heaviness
Feeding too fast causes nausea and bloating
after: Care for the mouth, even if the person does not eat by mouth
Wash and dry the skin around the gastrostomy every day
Keep notes: how much was given, stools, weight
See the doctor or nurse regularly
red_flags: Coughing, choking or wheezing during feeding: stop feeding; if it does not pass, call your local emergency number
The gastrostomy tube fell out: cover the opening with a clean gauze and see a doctor urgently, as the opening closes quickly
Vomiting blood or coffee-ground material, severe belly pain: call your local emergency number

faq.q: What if the tube is blocked?
faq.a: Try flushing with warm water using a syringe, without strong pressure. Do not clear it with a wire. If it does not work, call your doctor.

faq.q: Can I give food by mouth?
faq.a: Only if the doctor allowed it after checking swallowing. Otherwise food can go into the lungs.

reminders.text: Feeding soon. Formula at room temperature, person half sitting, flush the tube before and after.
